description: One entry per distinct PAGE SHAPE, not per route. Every `nodes` entry is a STRUCTURED OBJECT ({section, required, repeatable, variant?}), never a bare string, so `required` and `repeatable` are machine-enforceable rather than conventions a human has to remember.

nodeObjectShape.variant: optional string; present wherever the same section appears more than once on one page with different content rules

chromeNote: chrome.nav, chrome.footer and chrome.trial-modal are rendered ONCE by src/layout/Layout.jsx and are shared by every route; chrome.announcement-banner is rendered there too but gated per-route. They are listed as nodes on every template because a PageSpec describes a whole rendered page, but a page component must never re-declare them.
unmappedSectionsNote: Sections with no positional node in any template. These are not gaps: they are sections composed INSIDE another section rather than appearing as a page-level node. Each one's own contract records where.

T-PARTNER.reuseCorrection: CLONE_SPEC_CONTENT_B §8 calls these two feature rows 'the homepage's sections E and F verbatim'. THE MEASUREMENT DISAGREES: _reference/recon-b/partner_50pros.json blocks 3-5 and 8-10 show a DIFFERENT arrangement of the same assets and copy — a centred display heading block, then a centred copy block, then a two-column `mt-[9.5em] flex items-stretch justify-center` visual row — not the homepage's heading-in-the-right-column layout. sections/feature.seeds and sections/feature.report-csr are NOT reused here; a local FeatureSection in PartnerPage.jsx implements it.
T-PARTNER.bandColourEvidenceGap: EVIDENCE GAP, recorded rather than resolved. The FIRST divider band on this template is bg-cream-dark in the clone, but the section ABOVE it (hero.partner) is bg-cream — which contradicts the otherwise-universal 'band follows the section above' rule. The source's own justifying comment ('they follow a cream-dark section') is wrong about its own first band. The raw recon does NOT capture divider band fill (the divider <section> measures transparent and the band <div> is not in the `sections` tree), so the measurement cannot settle it either way. compatibility/graph.json therefore carries this as a NAMED, warn-severity exception rather than asserting a value.
